goal: Verify exact runtime source bytes before covered application code, routes, tools, recovery pages, historic forwarders, JSON route data, and transitive local scripts are served or executed.

trust_model.reason: A browser document cannot verify its own bytes before execution. A-003 therefore names one explicit bootstrap root and verifies every downstream covered source from it.
trust_model.verified_offline_policy: only previously verified bytes with the same expected hash may be used

phases.P0: Freeze A-002 head, verify main baseline, prepare manifest generator and inventory probe.
phases.P1: Generate current runtime integrity closure and identify external sources and unresolved executable paths.
phases.P2: Install bootstrap verification, integrity Service Worker, manifest-aware resolver, and Current Map integrity contract.
phases.P3: Generate and commit the exact final integrity manifest; seal its SHA-256 into the bootstrap root.
phases.P4: Run repository tests for valid bytes, one-byte tamper rejection, unlisted executable rejection, verified offline fallback, historical Home verification, and external-source policy.
phases.P5: Run live Chromium cold-start, controlled-runtime, six-screen, tool, recovery, historic, tamper, offline, and Service Worker matrices.
phases.P6: Issue final A-003 receipt and stop before merging A-002.

forbidden_effects: No claim that the root trust anchor self-verifies
stop_conditions: A-002 head or main baseline mismatch
Any runtime executable source cannot be assigned an exact expected digest or explicit trust classification
Any valid current route fails under enforcement
Any one-byte tamper is allowed to execute
Any unlisted HTML, JavaScript, JSON, module, worker, or WebAssembly source is served as executable
Integrity enforcement clears or rewrites user data
